newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta shares end higher on Telkom.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta shares end higher on Telkom.

text.p: Heavyweight Telkom's continued rise in late trading on Thursday helped the Jakarta Composite Index to close higher, brokers said.

Despite a sharp fall in the Dow Jones industrial average in New York overnight, which dampened sentiment in the region, keen buying interest in Telkom helped offset continued profit taking in some secondaries, including banking stocks.
The Jakarta Composite Index rose 1.33 points, or 0.21 percent, to end at 627.90 after touching an intra-day low of 625.92 points.
Decliners led advancers by 61 to 47, with 58 counters unchanged. Total volume was 220.78 million shares with a turnover of 481.4 billion rupiah.
Brokers said the market was likely to be mixed on Friday on follow-through profit taking and a lack of fresh local leads.
"Some overseas investors are preparing for the holiday season and are only trading for short-term gains," a broker with foreign firm said.
But brokers said support from local investors in some medium and small-capitalised stocks, which appeared to grow stronger recently, could give the market a positive tone.
"Local-led buying in some issues, including newly-listed counters, could help lift sentiment," a local broker said.
Telecommunications firm Telkom rose 125 rupiah to 3,975 on a volume of 6.6 million shares on what brokers said was fresh buying, boosted by its higher close in New York overnight.
Banking stocks, including Bank Negara Indonesia, Bank Umum Servitia and Bank International Indonesia, were among the targets of profit-takers, brokers said.
Bank Negara Indonesia topped the active list with 24.5 million shares being traded, falling 25 rupiah to 1,325 rupiah. Bank Umum Servitia fell 25 rupiah to 1,100 on 5.3 million shares.
